# A03-S01: Training rationale

Correspondence extract. [████] marks redaction; […] marks omission.

[…]

Hej [████]

I am not at all disagreeing, but I also do not quite understand where the concern
comes from. It also makes me a bit sad. Let me try to explain.

The dialogue I have made as a presentation text is quite down-to-earth
and everyday language. Besides, it is not written by Julina, whom I am going
to train first, but is part of the construction of the political
party and Julina. These will be two different tracks so I can contribute
as strongly as possible and in the different contexts that the project is
situated in.

Maybe it is because of the short text I sent earlier today. You
asked for a text for the wall, where I should explain my artistic
choices. I wrote that quickly, and I used a couple of technical terms. This is because the
explanatory genre requires me to speak as [████], i.e. from my
artistic expertise. That's just how I am, and it is not to be elitist, but
because it refers to the art historical terminology, i.e. to who has
done something similar before. If it becomes too demanding, then we
don't have to show this 'meta'-layer. We can show the work at eye level, as it
is, and where one can wonder if it is an AI or a human
who writes. That is why I use the fiction Computer Lars as
artist identity and Julina's future creator instead of myself. Lars
is just a LARS ;-)

We have agreed on the job title 'artist in residence' and not
'consultant', although I also suggested such a role. That means that
the public will judge our project based on artistic
criteria. You must trust that I know how to build such criteria so that
we do not get hit from that side. Because we would get that if the project
was not in dialogue with the art historical traditions, which exist in relation to
technology and politics. As artist in residence, I have artistic responsibility
for the product, and then I have to base it on my practice and the
techniques I have experience with, because the assessment of the work reflects
back on my integrity as an artist. Otherwise, we must redefine it as a
development task of a chatbot, which can then be part of MindFuture's
promotion strategy, as a kind of advertising, and not a work of art.

As I also told at our last meeting, I am currently fine-tuning
Julina on the most popular material at all – statements from the parties
seeking voter declarations. These are ordinary people's
formulations of their political wishes and dreams. It will speak
with spelling mistakes, capital letters, passionate reasonings, and give an unprecedented
insight into the part of the voter base that CANNOT be represented by
mainstream parties. There an AI can speak from. And that is the product
that you will have available afterward. But it must not be
a caricature or demagogue, because that is not in line with the
eighteenth global goal, I cannot stand behind that, nor have I
promised that. It must be a real and artistically challenging take on what
AI can be used for politically. And it should behave like an
AI, not as a human politician, that is, based on what
technology can do today and not in a streamlined version – it already
exists around New Zealand and Russia, which I have also explained
about.

If our product is to be defensible as a work of art and qua the designation
artist in residence be included as 'my' work, and get the quality that
is expected of my artistic signature, then I must also be allowed to
convey the difficult together with the simple, and have time to develop
the project through several tracks during the period.
